input.content: {"concept_id": "drv.motion.reverse_travel", "kind": "formula", "contract": "The road user is travelling rearward at the observation: the component of its velocity along the direction its body points is at most the negative of the reverse speed tolerance, a speed the caller sets, so that a rearward component smaller than it is read as none. The concept states the direction of the body's motion relative to the direction it points, at the observation only, and says nothing of how long the rearward motion lasts or where it happens. The whole of it is read from the road user's own velocity and the direction its body points, so no structure region, no device and no control state enters it. Not a stand-in for: the gear selected — a body in a forward gear rolls backwards on a grade and one in reverse stands still — a reversing lamp or any other signal, a halt, a turn, the place the motion happens at, or the component of the velocity along a structure region's designated direction of travel, which is a separate quantity read from the region and says nothing of the direction the body points.", "definition": null, "args": [{"name": "u", "sort": "track"}], "params": [{"name": "reverse_speed_tolerance", "unit": "m/s", "meaning": "the magnitude of the rearward velocity component below which the motion is not distinguished from a standing body's measurement noise; it names the source's resolution"}], "elements": [{"span": "the component of its velocity along the direction its body points", "atoms": ["kin.velocity", "kin.heading"], "concepts": [], "justification": "kin.velocity is the “velocity vector” in m/s in the world frame and kin.heading the “direction the body points”, which “a formula reads … normalised”, so the product of the two along the heading is the signed speed in the direction the body points.
